handbookNote: Mississippi Driver's License Manual, Revised December 2024, published by the Driver Service Bureau, Mississippi Department of Public Safety. Fetched directly as a PDF from the official Driver Service Bureau site (a dps.ms.gov subdomain) at driverservicebureau.dps.ms.gov/sites/default/files/2025-02/1.15.2025 Revised MDPS Driver's Manual.pdf, linked from the site's Learner's Permit and 'Download Driver License Manual' pages. Full text extracted with pdftotext and saved to temp/handbooks/ms/driver.txt (91-page manual, ~171KB text). Real exam mechanics: thoroughly researched across the fetched manual plus multiple official driverservicebureau.dps.ms.gov pages (Learner's Permit, Driver's Permit, Road Test, Classes A-D, frequently-asked-questions FAQ index, and two node pages) and the main dps.ms.gov site. CONFIRMED from the manual and site: the test is called the 'Computerized Exam,' is multiple-choice, must be taken in person (no cell phones/earbuds/smartwatches allowed in the testing area), and the minimum age to apply for a Learner's Permit (and take the exam) is fifteen years old. NOT found anywhere in the manual or on any official DPS/Driver Service Bureau page checked, including the FAQ: the exact number of questions on the knowledge test, the passing score/percentage, or whether the test is timed -- these are left explicitly UNCONFIRMED rather than guessed, consistent with this project's no-default-values rule. Content-depth rationale: this is an unusually detailed, numbers-rich 91-page manual (exact fees, distances in feet, DUI fine/jail/suspension tables, insurance minimums, speed limits by roadway type, reinstatement fees, etc.), comfortably supporting a large, non-repetitive, well-grounded 295-question bank across 22 topic buckets: licensing/GDL and the exam itself, vehicle equipment and the Squatted Vehicle Law, pavement markings and lane use, traffic signs, traffic signals and railroad crossings, speed/following distance, right-of-way and roundabouts, turning and lane changes, school buses and pedestrians, parking, night driving, seat belts and child restraints, DUI/alcohol/drugs and implied consent, insurance, license suspension/revocation/reinstatement, hazardous conditions and accidents, emergency vehicles and traffic stops, interstate driving and large vehicles, bicycles, distracted driving, general safe-driving basics, and organ donation/littering. The manual's own CLASS D / CDL section explicitly states that a Commercial Driver's License requires a separate knowledge and skills test based on the distinct 'Mississippi Professional Driver's Manual' -- so that commercial/CDL content was deliberately excluded from this bank, since it is not part of the standard Class R knowledge test this track represents. Price matches this project's established fixed Driver-track rate of $4.99 site-wide. Every question is grounded in a specific cited passage of the fetched official manual text; none are invented.
